findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Triple sink will be used in the meantime. Ensure dish machine is testing at the proper concentration to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is made at the proper concentration and is available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed open BBQ sauce that was not refrigerated after opening. Discussed with PIC, BBQ sauce was from the previous week. BBQ sauce was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly cold held after opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer portion of mop bucket. Ensure after use, mops are placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an opened ice tea container sitting on the edge of the hand wash sink. CORRECTED - PIC was informed and the ice tea container was moved to a different location. Ensure foods are not kept on the edge or around the hand wash sink to prevent possible contamination during hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several washed, rinsed and sanitized serving utensils to have food debris. PIC was informed and they were moved to the triple sink for cleaning. Ensure that any equipment used for food-contact surfaces and utensils are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an opened teriyaki glacé sauce, labeled “Refrigerate After Opening,” sitting on a shelf in the dry storage area. The PIC was informed and stated that the sauce would be discarded in two days after notifying the food manager, who was not present during the inspection. Inspectors will conduct a spot check on 01/22/2026 to ensure compliance. Ensure that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored at 5°C (41°F) or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT - Inspectors observed the following foods in the refrigerator to be missing date marks:
- Sliced boiled eggs
- Sliced tomatoes
- Pot roast
  
Discussed with PIC about the importance of date marking TCS foods. The inspectors will follow up with the facility on 01/22/2026 to ensure TCS foods are being date marked. Ensure that TCS foods prepared for more than 24 hours are date marked and discarded after a maximum of 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed light to be passing through the lower part of the back door by the triple sink. PIC was informed. Ensure that the gap at the door is sealed to prevent entry of insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed dishes and utensils placed on liners in the dish shelves and utensil drawers. The liners are made of an absorbent, cloth-like material, which can retain moisture and bacteria, making them unsafe for storing clean dishes and utensils. The PIC was informed and stated that the liners will be removed prior to the next routine inspection. Always ensure that surfaces that come into contact with clean dishes and utensils are smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with pink substance. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be properly cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed date marking to be missing on multiple TCS item within facility. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking procedure. Date marking stickers were placed on TCS items, ensure any TCS items that are opened and kept longer than 24 hours are date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed coffee machine to be soiled with rust. Discussed with PIC, coffee machine will be cleaned. Ensure food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents rust from forming.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer portion of mop bucket. Ensure after use, mops are placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed black mold to be present at triple sink caulking in kitchen. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/ replacing caulking as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, santizer bucket was set up and tested at 200 ppm (Quat). Ensure sanitizing solution is set up at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Inspector found priority and priority foundation violations during the inspection. Ensure that good food safety habits are formed that line up with code requirements. Inspector did a good deal of coaching during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Person cooking and in charge of the kitchen at Centennial point today is not a certified food protection manager (CFPM). Ensure that the person in charge of the facility kitchen holds a CFPM by the next routine inspection.

 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival the inspector was not able to dry hands due to a lack of disposable towels at the facility kitchen hand sink. The kitchen pic did not know how to procure towels for the hand sink. Replace hand towels as soon as the supply is exhausted. The pic fond the maintenance person who provided towels to the dispenser. Violation was corrected on site.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the coffee maker to be soiled around the water dispensing area above the filter basket. Clean and maintain clean. The piece of equipment was cleaned and sanitized at the time of inspection. The violation was corrected on site.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a lack of sanitation bucket upon entry to the facility. The facility had performed food preparation duties. Set up sanitizer at the start of each day and keep wet wiping cloths in the sanitizer between uses. A sanitizer bucket was provided and testes to be 400ppm of Quat.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed wet wiping cloths on the food prep table across from the cooking equipment and two on the edge of the three part sink. Store all wet wiping cloths properly in sanitizer between uses. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed knives stored in a holder which has soil on the top. Also the drawer holding utensils at the prep table has crumbs and food debris. Clean and maintain these areas clean so that they do not contaminate food contact surfaces. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the two door cooler on to have a cardboard box holding bags of carrots, cherries and other produce. Remove cardboard as it is not smooth and cleanable. Use smooth non absorbent easily cleanable surfaces in the facility.  

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the shelves under the prep table across from cooking equipment to have crumbs and food debris on it and the drip tray of the oven has an accumulation of food. Clean and maintain the area free of accumulated food debris.  
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the floor between the prep table and the wall to have an accumulation of soil and food debris. The floor between the fryer and stove and between the cooking equipment and the wall has soil grease starting to accumulate. Clean and maintain these areas free of accumulated soil. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a cigarette butt in the drip tray of the oven. The oven drip tray was cleaned immediately. Ensure that no one is smoking in the building especially in the kitchen.  

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the dish puck to read 155F indicating that the surfaces of items intended to be sanitized in the machine are not reaching the proper temperature for sanitation. Call has been placed for machine to be serviced/repaired. While machine is not functioning use the three part sink with sanitizer at manufacturers recommendations for concentrations and contact time. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cottage cheese and shredded cheese to be lacking date marking. Dates were added at time of inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a spray bottle labeled air freshener to be located next to single use forks. Store chemicals under the sink or next to the dish machine on shelves provided. Properly protect single use food items. The spray bottle was moved over under the sink for proper storage. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following non food contact items soiled with crumbs and food debris:
1) drawer edges
2) drip tray of the stove top
3) inside of fryer
4) bottoms of freezers
Clean and maintain these areas free of accumulated soil. 
Kitchen manager started cleaning immediately. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Floor under the dish machine is soiled. The rack of the machine is a hinderance to cleaning. Make extra effort to keep that area clean. Also the floor behind the oven and fryer has debris. A plastic bag and a paper party hat are observed. Clean the floors and maintain them clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed the following areas to be soiled:
1. The area of the table at the base of the can opener.
2. Top of the stove
3. Area between the stove top and fryer
Clean these ares more frequently and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Observed a can of soda on the prep table next to the fryer. Also observed a personal drink cup on the prep area next to clean utensils and coffee filters. Items were collected and placed in the area with personal items.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed a box of potatoes to be stored on the floor in the kitchen. Store food at least 6 inches above the floor. 
Observed the table with the hand sink in it to be used for preparation of dessert portions. A covered cake and portions of cake are very close to the hand sink and may be subject to splash during hand washing. Protect food from potential contamination at this area. The table was rearranged so that personal items are in this area and the cake prep will take place at the other end of the table.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Observed a box of styrofoam cups to be stored on the floor in the kitchen. Store clean items at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

It is observed during the inspection that hooks provided for the storage of employee coats and other personal items are hanging off of the end of a shelf holding food and food related items along with clean aprons. Provide appropriate storage space that does not compromise items that are intended to be clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the interior baffles of both ice machines (Centennial Pointe and the Arbors) to have accumulation of mold build-up (brown and pink molds). Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. PIC is adding cleaning that area to the weekly list at both locations - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/22/22.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no heat test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer for the heated dish machine (two sets will be needed for each location when the Arbors is operational). Discussed with PIC. PIC is ordering heat test strips. Inspector will follow-up on 7/8/22.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no working sani bucket during the inspection. Employee stated that none had been made this morning and both breakfast and lunch service had been completed. A sani bucket should be made prior to food engagement. Ensure all staff is aware. A sani bucket of quaternary ammonium was made - 400 ppm. Test strips available. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed baffle of the ice machine to have mold build-up. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Inspector showed PIC where mold was building inside the ice machine - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

Observed the hand sink nearest the dish machine on the Arbor’s side of the facility to not have hot water and barely come from the faucet. Repair this hand sink so pressure is adequate as well as temperature of hot water. Inspector will follow-up on 11/1/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed the mop on the Centennial Pointe side of the facility to not be stored properly in the mop/utility sink. Ensure mops may air and/or drip dry. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed multiple areas in need of re-caulking:
1. Both dish machines at each kitchen need recaulking either due to mold build-up and/or missing caulk.
2. All 4 employee bathrooms (2 on each side) need re-caulked hand sinks. Caulking is cracked.

Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed mold still present on the interior baffle of the ice machine at the Arbors side of the facility. Discussed wash, rinse, and sanitize. Inspector is following up on 7/29/21.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

(REPEAT) Observed ice dumped in Centennial Pointe kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC that hand washing sink is for hand washing only - no dumping. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/6/20. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed both kitchen’s to have mold on the interior baffles of the ice machines. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC’s. Wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 7/19/21.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed stacks of single-use articles on top shelf in Centennial Pointe kitchen to not be inverted to prevent cross contamination - food- and lip-contact surfaces should be inverted. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

(REPEAT) Observed no test strips for bleach. Observed no maximum registering thermometer and/or heat test strips. Both kitchen’s should have these items, as well as the quaternary ammonium test strips. Purchase items. Inspector will follow-up on 7/19/21. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/6/20.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for food employee’s who are not CFPM’s. Discussed need for licensure with PIC. Keep copies within a public health binder or folder.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed no allergen training completed by CFPM’s. Discussed need for all certified food protection manager’s to have allergen training. Provided copy of training information. Keep certificates in a public health binder. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/6/20.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

Facility lacked Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Provided paperwork. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by ice. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed dumped ice within hand washing sink. Hand sinks are designated for hand washing only. Discussed importance of only using sink for hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer bucket was unavailable at beginning of inspection. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed no working bucket of quat at beginning of inspection. Employee explained process to sanitize food contact surface: dish water and soap with rag. Discussed need for bleach and/or quat to sanitize food contact surfaces. Facility staff was able to find quat and create a sani bucket. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed in-use wiping cloth to be stored outside of sanitization bucket. Discussed need for in-use clothes to be immersed within sanitization buckets at all times with appropriate concentrations. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed no maximizing register thermometer and/or heat test strips for the dish machine that utilizes heat to sanitize. Discussed need for equipment with PIC in order to maintain appropriate temperatures of the dish machine. Follow-up will be conducted on 1/16/20.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Currently this has not taken place. Hand out was given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed quat sanitizer bucket in The Arbors kitchen to have a concentration less than 200ppm. CORRECTED- Sanitizer jug was replaced for the wall-mounted dispenser and bucket was remade.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand soap not provided at hand sink near the dish machine located in the Arbors kitchen. 
->Provide liquid soap at all hand washing sinks for adequate handwashing. Hand soap restocked at the time of inspection. Reference 6-301.11.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The following items were noted in establishment beyond the discard date mark: Sour cream (3/18) located in the 1 door upright in the Alf kitchen. Sour cream (3/18), whole milk (3/23), chocolate milk (3/18) located in the arbors walk-in cooler. Items discarded. 
->Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in the wiping buckets in the Arbor kitchen measured with concentrations less than 150 ppm. Wiping clothes were noted stored in solution at the time of inspection. 
-> Wiping cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Please verify solutions and change as needed to ensure proper concentrations. Reference 3-304.14.
